selection_contract.source_universe: Official or first-party records responsive to the exact missing denominator, selection, rights, transaction, and recovery predicates declared by SSC-W01-MR01.

records.title: 2026 NatSec100 report and methodology
normalized_fact_record: Publishes a complete selected roster of 100 ranked companies for the 2026 edition.
Uses a proprietary weighted model with U.S. government contracting activity, recent capital raised, total capital raised, and recent headcount growth as disclosed inputs.

Requires venture or private-equity backing, no public listing or filed IPO, no acquisition by a public company, public defense or dual-use applicability, at least one U.S. government contract by December 31 2025, and FOCI vetting.
Explains SpaceX exclusion under the IPO rule and describes Anthropic as formally evaluated but ineligible at publication during an active contract dispute and litigation.
States that signals are not outcomes and acknowledges public-data, classified-work, valuation, and operational-impact limits.
limitations: Does not disclose the complete candidate universe, exact weights, rejected-company rows, or FOCI decisions.
Ranking inclusion does not prove technical superiority, procurement causation, investment causation, or common purpose.
The published roster is a first-party selected denominator, not an independently reproduced candidate denominator.

records.title: SBA and DoD celebrate first year of SBICCT
normalized_fact_record: Reports 22 formal SBICCT applications since launch and 13 funds approved for Green Light or licensing as of October 22 2024.
States that 12 firms managed the 13 funds and planned $2.8 billion in private capital matched with SBA-guaranteed loans.
States that licensees could access up to $175 million in SBA-guaranteed leverage and program-related DoD benefits.
limitations: Does not name all 22 applicants or the nine applications not in the 13-fund approved group.
Does not disclose applicant scoring, per-fund leverage commitments, realized returns, failures, or recovery.
The October 2024 denominator is time-bounded and does not describe later cohorts.

records.title: First 18 SBIC Critical Technologies Initiative funds
normalized_fact_record: Declares the entire first cohort to contain 18 Licensed or Green Light Approved funds.
States that 17 fund names are shown in the official graphic and one Green Light fund withheld its name under SBA policy.
States that seven funds were fully licensed and had begun investing.
Reports more than 100 funds had expressed interest and that diligence had begun on a second cohort.
Projects more than $4 billion of investment across more than 1,700 portfolio companies.
limitations: Does not disclose the complete applicant and rejection denominator for the first or second cohort.
The 17 names are presented in a graphic and are not separately transcribed in this supplement.
Projections are not realized deployment, returns, public benefit, or repayment.

records.title: SBICCT Investment Policy Statement
normalized_fact_record: Defines the joint SBA and DoD portfolio objectives and governance framework for SBICCT.
Covers strategic sectors, stages, asset allocation, portfolio construction, licensee management, risk management, monitoring, and reporting.
Records that the initiative began accepting SBIC licensure applications on September 29 2023.
limitations: Portfolio-level governance does not disclose per-fund selection scores, leverage commitments, returns, failures, or recovery.
Policy rules do not establish how every selected fund performed.

records.title: Manage an SBIC: leverage and repayment terms
normalized_fact_record: Describes standard-debenture leverage as typically no more than two times private capital, with a ten-year term and stated fees.
Describes accrual-debenture leverage and repayment obligations tied to distributions to private investors.
Requires leverage proceeds to be used for qualifying small-business investments.
limitations: These are general SBIC terms and do not establish the exact instrument or commitment for any SBICCT fund.
General repayment priority does not establish realized public recovery or fund performance.

records.title: 89 FR 79271: OSC equipment-finance Notice of Funding Availability
records.publisher: Office of the Federal Register / Department of Defense
normalized_fact_record: Makes up to $984 million available for direct equipment-finance loans in 31 covered technology categories.
Sets expected loan sizes from $10 million to $150 million and anticipates approximately ten successful applicants.
Uses a two-stage process and identifies statutory compliance, national or economic security impact, project additionality, and creditworthiness among selection criteria.
limitations: Does not identify applicants, invitees to the second stage, selected or rejected rows, or negotiated loan terms.
The planned approximate award count is not the observed final denominator.

records.title: OSC receives $8.9 billion in manufacturing financing requests
normalized_fact_record: Reports more than 200 applications totaling $8.9 billion against $984 million in current lending capacity.
Reports applicants from 38 states across sizes, stages, and sectors, with requests from $10 million to $150 million.
States that applications were under review and selected applicants were expected later in 2025.
limitations: Does not identify applicants, selection scores, second-stage invitees, selected or rejected rows, or terms.
Application demand does not establish favoritism, capture, effectiveness, or complete public benefit.

records.title: OSC Credit Program current status
normalized_fact_record: States that the September 27 2024 equipment-finance Part 1 window closed on February 3 2025.
States that OSC continues to engage directly with existing applicants and is no longer accepting Part 1 submissions for the first NOFA.
Describes direct debt financing for eligible borrowers in critical technology areas.
limitations: Does not publish the applicant roster, second-stage invitees, award denominator, rejected rows, or complete agreements.
A current program-status page does not prove disbursement, milestones, defaults, or recovery.

records.title: OSC first direct loan to MP Materials
normalized_fact_record: Reports execution of a $150 million direct loan to MP Materials for heavy rare-earth separation capacity at Mountain Pass, California.
Identifies the transaction as OSC’s first direct loan and links it to July 2025 legislation providing credit-subsidy funding.
Names the borrower, amount, facility, and intended use.
limitations: Does not publish the complete loan agreement, pricing, security, covenants, disbursement schedule, performance, defaults, or recovery history.
Does not establish that MP Materials was selected from the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

records.title: OSC conditional commitments to Vulcan Elements and ReElement Technologies
normalized_fact_record: Reports separate conditional loan commitments of $620 million to Vulcan Elements and $80 million to ReElement Technologies.
States that the Department will receive warrants from both companies and that Commerce proposed incentives and equity for Vulcan.
States that no OSC funds are disbursed until financial, legal, technical, and other conditions are completed.
limitations: Conditional commitments are not executed loans or disbursements.
Does not publish the complete agreements, warrant terms, valuation, milestones, defaults, or recovery.
Does not establish that either company was selected from the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

records.title: OSC conditional commitment to Phoenix Tailings
normalized_fact_record: Reports a $500 million conditional loan commitment to Phoenix Tailings for domestic rare-earth processing.
States that OSC financing plus additional private capital are intended to provide approximately $1 billion.
States that financial, legal, technical, and other due diligence remains before financial close.
limitations: Conditional commitment is not an executed loan or disbursement.
Does not publish the complete agreement, private-capital denominator, milestones, defaults, or recovery.
Does not establish relation to the first equipment-finance NOFA applicant universe.

records.title: OSC conditional commitment to Energy Fuels
normalized_fact_record: Reports a $725 million conditional loan commitment to Energy Fuels for domestic rare-earth processing.
States that financial, legal, technical, and other due diligence remains before financial close.
Reports that OSC had committed more than $5 billion in FY26 debt financing and mobilized more than $11 billion in total public and private capital.
limitations: Conditional commitment is not an executed loan or disbursement.
The named transactions in this supplement do not exhaust the reported FY26 aggregate.
Does not publish the complete agreement, milestones, defaults, recovery, or relation to the first NOFA applicant universe.
